sections.h2: How does selling a house in Delaware, Ohio work?
sections.html:
Delaware sellers list with an agent, sell by owner, or take a cash offer, and in all three cases the deed moves through the Delaware County Auditor and Recorder. Delaware is the county seat, set on the Olentangy River along U.S. Route 23 north of Columbus. It is one of the faster-growing cities in the group: the Census Bureau estimates 46,636 people for July 2025, up 12.9 percent from the 2020 estimates base of 41,297.

That growth shapes the sale. New subdivisions compete with older homes near downtown, and buyers arrive from the Columbus area with different budgets. The city's own fast-facts page says Delaware attracts people looking for affordability, lower income taxes, good schools and small town living.

sections.h2: What is Delaware's story, and does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
It matters mainly for the older housing near downtown and the university. The city was built on the site of a Mingo village called Pluggy's Town, and the town plan was filed in 1808. In 1812, Delaware lost the vote to become Ohio's capital by a single vote to Columbus.

Railroads arrived in 1851, and Ohio Wesleyan University was founded in 1844. The university still anchors downtown along South Sandusky Street, and the city says its downtown is 94 percent occupied.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Delaware homes?
sections.html:
Delaware is a majority-owner city with a median home value of $318,400. These figures are the Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020 through 2024.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing: $318,400.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 64.7 percent across 16,728 households, averaging 2.57 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,286; median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,892.
  • Median household income: $99,786; share of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 47.8 percent.
  • Mean travel time to work: 25.6 minutes.
  • Residents under 18: 23.8 percent; residents 65 and older: 14.7 percent.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve houses in Delaware?
sections.html:
Three public school districts reach into the city limits, so the district on your address can differ from your neighbor's. The city's fast-facts page describes each at its approximate scale.

Public school districts within Delaware city limits (source: City of Delaware fast facts)
DistrictApproximate studentsCity's description
Delaware City School DistrictAbout 6,000The historic city district
Olentangy Local School DistrictOver 24,000Covers a large area across several jurisdictions
Buckeye Valley School DistrictAround 2,300Smaller district reaching the city

The Delaware City district's high school is Rutherford B. Hayes High School, and its middle school is John C. Dempsey Middle School. Look up your parcel before naming a district in a listing.

sections.h2: Which roads and employers connect Delaware to the region?
sections.html:
U.S. Routes 23, 36 and 42 pass through the city, and Ohio Route 37 crosses it east to west. The Delaware Municipal Airport lies southwest of the central business district.

The city says no single sector dominates its economy. Its top employers include Kroger grocery and distribution at about 2,496 jobs, Ohio Wesleyan University at 1,571, Delaware County government at 1,114, OhioHealth at 1,022 and Delaware City Schools at 996. The list also includes automotive parts distribution, manufacturing and health care. The same page says many local graduates rent for a time and buy once they have families.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules should a Delaware seller know?
sections.html:
The city's Planning and Community Development Department enforces zoning and property maintenance, and its Building Division is a state-certified building department. Its FAQ answers several questions a seller or buyer will hit.

  • Structural, electrical or mechanical work likely needs a permit; so do fences, decks, sheds, garages and additions. Patios do not.
  • Starting in 2026, contractors no longer need to register with the city.
  • All vehicles, including trailers, must be parked on a hard surface such as asphalt, concrete or existing gravel; new or expanded gravel parking is not allowed.
  • Signs in the right-of-way, tree lawns and on utility poles are prohibited and are removed by code enforcement.

Violation notices are posted on the property, and vacant properties get a mailed notice to the owner listed with the county auditor. If a violation is not corrected in time, the city can fix it and bill the owner, and an unpaid bill can become a lien or be added to the property tax bill. The city can also recommend criminal or civil charges. Deal with notices before you list, since a buyer's title search will see a lien.

sections.h2: What does Delaware County do on valuation, deeds and recording?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 triennial valuation update is the main date a Delaware owner should know. The Auditor's page says the informal review period has ended and that a formal complaint against a valuation can be filed with the Board of Revision from January 1, 2027, through March 31, 2027. The complaint form is on the Auditor's forms page, which also carries the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, form DTE 100. Ask the Auditor's office for the conveyance fee rate that applies to your sale.

The Recorder handles the deed after that. Its fee page lists $39 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage, which includes a $5 preservation surcharge, and $8 for each additional page. The office is at 145 N. Union Street, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a 4:00 p.m. cutoff for document submission. Fees on a county page can change, so confirm them before you send a check.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require a Delaware seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the owner of a one-to-four-unit residential property to complete the state disclosure form and give the buyer a signed copy. A buyer who first receives the form, or an amendment, after signing the contract may rescind in writing within three business days, and no later than the sooner of thirty days after acceptance or closing.

The statute covers sale, land installment contract, lease with option to purchase and exchange. A seller who inherited the house and has not lived in it for a year is excluded, along with transfers between spouses or to family in the direct line.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale worth a look in Delaware?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when speed or condition matters more than the highest price. A house with deferred repairs, a notice from code enforcement, tenants, or an estate to settle can be hard to list. A buyer purchasing as-is skips the showings and the repair negotiations.

Compare any cash figure with a realistic list price less repairs, the months of carrying cost, and the property tax bill still accruing. Keep the written terms for price, closing date and closing costs for each offer in one place.

faqs.q: When can I file a complaint about my Delaware County valuation?
faqs.a: The informal review period for the 2026 triennial update has ended. The Auditor's page says a formal complaint can be filed with the Board of Revision beginning January 1, 2027, and no later than March 31, 2027, using the form on the Auditor's forms page.

faqs.q: Which projects need a permit in Delaware?
faqs.a: Fences, decks, sheds, garages and home additions need permits, and so does any structural, electrical or mechanical work. Patios do not. Ask the Building Division what is needed to close an unpermitted structure before listing.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a city violation notice?
faqs.a: The city can correct the problem and bill you, and an unpaid bill may become a lien or be added to the property tax bill. It can also recommend criminal or civil charges through the city prosecutor.

faqs.q: Where is the Delaware County Recorder and what does it charge?
faqs.a: The Recorder is at 145 N. Union Street in Delaware. Its fee page lists $39 for the first two pages of a deed, which includes a $5 preservation surcharge, and $8 for each additional page.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Delaware home in?
faqs.a: It could be Delaware City, Olentangy Local or Buckeye Valley, since all three reach into the city. Confirm by parcel with the county or the district before you name one in a listing.
